question: L0 requires the whole of conformance/vectors/reason-codes.json. Five of its 21 cases (RC-003, RC-010..RC-013) are about failed_checks, which the registry scopes to 'federation trust evaluation' — an L3 concern, and L0 requires no federation capability. Must an L0 implementation pass those five cases?
classification_note: Not MISSING_RULE: reading (a) — a required vector file means all of its cases — is complete and is what the registry's plain text says, and under it every case is determinable. Not DISCOVERABILITY: the answer is not somewhere else in the package, it is absent. Two defensible readings survive, and they differ in how much an L0 implementation must build, so AMBIGUITY is the honest class. operator-manifests.json carries a per-case certification_level and the other two files do not, which is what makes the second reading available at all.
resolution: RESOLVED. Original classification AMBIGUITY preserved. Resolved on the normative surface by required_vector_cases in the conformance-profile registry: L0 takes 9 of the 21 reason-code cases; the 12 concerning failed_checks, trust_status, receipt equivalence and per-step engine statuses belong to L3. No vector file was split or rewritten and the case grammars are untouched. Re-run against package be9adfe1fdf7d590: the L0 obligation is 49 cases, read from the registry rather than inferred.

question: The profile registry requires capabilities named consumer_payment, merchant_acceptance, transfer, traceability, payment_request, payment_initiation, instant_execution, cross_operator_routing, reconciliation, inter_operator_settlement, external_acquiring. The capabilities schema declares supports_wallets, supports_qr, supports_traces, supports_federation and so on. The operator manifest's capabilities array is a free-form string list whose examples are hyphenated ('payment-intents', 'qr', 'federation'). Three vocabularies. How does an implementation declare that it has capability 'traceability'?
classification_note: Nine of the eleven profile-registry capability names appear nowhere in the package outside the registry itself. No mapping is published in any artefact, so the required behaviour — declaring a capability the profile requires — cannot be performed from the package. It is not AMBIGUITY: there are not two readings, there is no reading. Out of scope for the L0 verdict because L0's required_capabilities is empty, but it blocks L1 and above.
resolution: RESOLVED. Original classification MISSING_RULE preserved: it was one. Resolved by contracts/production/capability-registry.production.json (one canonical namespace, every supports_* flag audited individually, one alias registered on demonstrated equivalence) and spec/capabilities.md (declaration semantics, exact comparison, no implicit normalisation), with 12 vectors in conformance/vectors/capabilities.json. Re-run against package be9adfe1fdf7d590: the §6 procedure decides all 12 vectors from the package alone, 0 divergent.

resolution: Resolved from the package alone: the vectors are present; the reference is redundant here.
